purpose: Stable knowledge for explaining why new players, including PoE2-first players, get stuck in PoE1 and what PathcraftAI can concretely fill.

source_references.evidence: Official overview says skills are socketed gems, up to five support gems can affect a skill, the passive tree is vast, maps have modifiers, and the game is built around itemized systems.
Support gems must be in linked sockets on the same item to benefit active skill gems, which supports the PoE2-to-PoE1 socket/link mismatch diagnosis.
Official item filter syntax exposes linked socket groups and socket colors, showing that links/colors are important enough to be filterable beginner upgrade targets.
PoE Vault describes PoE as daunting even for ARPG players because many complex systems interlock and recommends Path of Building as an external tool.
PoE Vault states support gems do nothing if not linked to an active skill gem, matching a common new player failure mode.
Elemental resistances are capped at 75%, and excess resistance can buffer curses or resistance reduction.
Beginner passive tree advice recommends following build guides, not deviating early, and notes refund points/Orb of Regret costs.
League starter builds are described as early-start functional, low/no-currency, and accessible; the site also warns that melee and bow archetypes are usually harder to gear/execute.
A beginner-help thread explicitly calls out PoE2-to-PoE1 socket/link confusion and gives early survival checkpoints such as life, armour/evasion, and 75% elemental resistances.
A new player reports being overwhelmed after campaign because guides assume Harvest, Essence, Eldritch Altars, and other mechanics; replies recommend narrowing focus to simple mechanics first.
Community discussion reinforces that beginner guides often require repeated review, third-party tools, and many new concepts.

summary.core_problem: PoE1 is primarily knowledge-gated. New players usually fail because the game gives many irreversible-looking choices, weak explanations, and delayed feedback about whether a build, item, map, or farming plan is viable.
summary.product_principle: Do not teach everything at once. Detect the user's current wall, hide irrelevant advanced systems, and return the next 3 concrete actions.

expected_mismatch: PoE2 players often expect smoother enemy scaling and clearer combat readability.
PoE2 skill gems live in a skill interface; PoE1 power is heavily tied to gear sockets, socket colors, and linked sockets.
PoE2 map/waystone expectations do not transfer cleanly to PoE1 map mods, reflect, sustain, Atlas bonus, and league mechanic risk.
PoE2 players may know ARPG combat, but not PoE1-specific defenses, flask setup, ailment immunity, crafting, and economy heuristics.
poe2_to_poe1.tone: Translate differences without implying the user is bad. Assume the player has game sense but lacks PoE1-specific mental models.

expected_mismatch: Passive tree size creates choice paralysis.
Players do not know which build guide is league-start safe.
Support gems, sockets, links, colors, item levels, affixes, prefixes, and suffixes are introduced before the player can judge value.
The campaign hides many future failure checks until maps expose weak defenses or bad damage scaling.
poe1_first_timer.tone: Reduce scope aggressively. Explain only what changes the next play session.

friction_points.why_players_get_stuck: Too many skills, passives, supports, league mechanics, and currencies are available before the player knows what matters.
symptoms: reads many guides but cannot choose
pathcraft_can_fill: Pick one build lane and suppress irrelevant options.
Show only the next 3 actions.
Label each recommendation as required, useful, or optional.

friction_points.why_players_get_stuck: A build can look fun but require uniques, currency, levels, or mechanics the player cannot access yet.
symptoms: guide says cheap but gear is unavailable
pathcraft_can_fill: Detect required uniques, 6-link dependency, attribute gaps, and main skill transition level from PoB.
Warn when a build is not league-start safe.
Suggest a temporary bridge skill instead of forcing the final build too early.

friction_points.why_players_get_stuck: PoE1 support gems only work when linked to the active skill on the same gear piece, while PoE2 players are used to skill-gem-centric support sockets.
symptoms: support gem equipped but no damage change
pathcraft_can_fill: Render a slot-by-slot gem link plan.
Explain whether the current main skill is actually linked to its supports.
Give color/socket priority for the next gear upgrade.

friction_points.why_players_get_stuck: The passive tree is large, path-dependent, and attribute/connection requirements can block respecs.
symptoms: tree path looks different from guide
pathcraft_can_fill: Compare current PoB tree to target stages.
Identify missing path nodes or attribute requirements.
Give a safe respec order instead of only showing the final tree.

friction_points.why_players_get_stuck: PoE1 deaths often come from missing resistance caps, chaos resistance, ailment immunity, flask suffixes, recovery, map mods, or defensive layers rather than one obvious mistake.
symptoms: campaign was fine but maps kill me
does not know what killed them
pathcraft_can_fill: Show stage-specific defense checkpoints.
Flag deadly map mods for the build.
Prioritize the weakest defensive slot first.

friction_points.area: Map mods, Atlas, and league mechanic overload
friction_points.why_players_get_stuck: Maps introduce reflect, no regen, reduced recovery, minus max resistance, dangerous rare stacks, and league mechanics at the same time as Atlas progression.
symptoms: can kill bosses but dies to league mechanic
does not know which map mods to reroll
does not know whether to farm or progress
pathcraft_can_fill: Generate build-specific map regex.

Classify farming readiness from Atlas progress, comfortable highest tier, death rate, clear speed, voidstones, and investment recovery. Treat Atlas 100 and T16 under 2 minutes as local benchmarks only.
Recommend one main mechanic and one support mechanic, not every mechanic.

friction_points.area: Crafting, affixes, trade, and item value
friction_points.why_players_get_stuck: Players do not know which drops are valuable, which affixes matter, when to craft, or when to buy.
symptoms: does not know how to fix gear
pathcraft_can_fill: Translate affixes into build value.
Give slot-by-slot craft recipes by stage.
Mark currency as spend now, save, or trade.

friction_points.why_players_get_stuck: PoE1 often expects Path of Building, loot filters, trade search, price checking, regex, and wiki lookup before the player understands the core loop.
symptoms: does not know what to import
cannot turn a guide into actions
pathcraft_can_fill: Import PoB and explain it in plain Korean.
Convert long guide data into checklist steps.
Generate loot filter and map regex outputs without teaching the whole toolchain first.

friction_points.why_players_get_stuck: PoE1 combat can become visually noisy, especially inside dense league mechanics, so new players cannot identify the dangerous source.
symptoms: does not know what killed them
gets tired faster than in PoE2
pathcraft_can_fill: Recommend safer mechanics until defenses improve.
List visual danger signs and map mods for the selected mechanic.
Offer conservative farming alternatives when the build is not ready for density.

coach_rules: Always identify at most 3 likely friction points for the current build/user state.
If the user came from PoE2, include PoE2-to-PoE1 translation notes for sockets/links, map mods, visual density, and crafting.
Do not dump an encyclopedia. Return next actions that can be completed in the next session.

Prefer checklists with measurable signals: resistance cap, life/ES, main link count, Atlas progress, comfortable highest tier, death rate, T16 clear time, voidstones. Do not present Atlas 100 or T16 under 2 minutes as official gates.
When information is missing, ask for one measurement instead of assuming the player is ready for advanced farming.

fillable_features_backlog.description: Hide advanced sections and show current wall, next 3 actions, and must-not-do warnings.
Translate skill gems, sockets, supports, map mods, flasks, and atlas expectations for PoE2-first players.
Ask map tier/mods, resistances, chaos resistance, ailment immunity, and flask setup, then return likely causes.
Detect required links, uniques, attributes, ailment immunity, and DPS floor from PoB.
Use Atlas progress, comfortable highest tier, death rate, T16 clear time, voidstones, and investment recovery to classify early/mid/late mapping. Hard thresholds are local calibration only.
Explain Essence, Harvest, Expedition, Legion, Breach, Delirium, Ritual, and Blight by risk, reward, and build fit.
